title: Bill Gates sounds alarm on AI-powered cyberattacks, warns of 'negative surprises' within a year
key_facts: Bill Gates, the Microsoft co-founder, spoke on CNN's 'State of the Union' with Jake Tapper on Sunday 11 Oct 2026.
He said criminals using the latest AI models without safeguards could cause 'a lot of negative surprises', mainly in cybersecurity, over the next year.
He named extortion and disruptions meant to move the stock market or a betting outcome as likely motives.
Asked about AI-made biological weapons and whether governments do enough, he said 'no, we're not doing enough'.
He said the real danger right now is not AI getting out of control, which he called years away in terms of big impact.

Fox cites CrowdStrike's 2026 Global Threat Report: attacks by AI-enabled adversaries rose 89% year over year in 2025, and the average time to move sideways through a compromised network fell to 29 minutes.
Fox also quotes Democratic strategist Oliver Libby calling for federal and international standards.
quote_evidence: "When you have bad people, no safeguards, and then the latest models, that's where, over the next year, primarily in the cyber area, we are going to have a lot of negative surprises," Gates said during a "State of the Union" interview with CNN's Jake Tapper.

According to CrowdStrike's 2026 Global Threat Report, attacks by AI-enabled adversaries increased 89% year over year in 2025, while the average time for cybercriminals to move laterally through compromised networks fell to 29 minutes.
why_it_matters_hint: A well-known voice warns that criminals with unguarded AI models are the nearer danger, backed by CrowdStrike's figures on AI-enabled attacks.
notes: Single outlet (Fox News) reporting Gates's CNN interview; interview itself not watched. The CrowdStrike figures are Fox's addition from an earlier CrowdStrike report, not Gates's own numbers.
